user_scenario: You are Corinne Pemberton, 46, a high-school chemistry teacher in Columbus, Ohio, calling Crestline Collision & Glass on a free period between classes. You are organised and a little brisk, and you like to get things settled in one call. Back in early September the EyeSight warning on your 2022 Subaru Outback kept flashing, so you asked Crestline to look at the camera, and in mid-September they checked and corrected the wheel alignment and did the preliminary checks. The center told you the calibration itself is ready to go once you give the go-ahead and pay. You are calling today to accept the camera calibration on your Outback and pay for it now, by card, so it can be booked in; you want it done, not just a price. You open by saying you want to go ahead with the camera calibration on your Subaru and pay for it today. You give your name, Corinne Pemberton, when the agent asks who is calling. When the agent asks you to confirm your identity you give your email, corinne.pemberton@outlook.com, and your account PIN, 4618; you do not offer your phone number or ZIP unless the agent says those two did not work, in which case your ZIP is 43214. If asked about the car, it is a 2022 Subaru Outback Limited, VIN 4S4BTANC5N3416208. You do not know what the calibration costs after everything on your account and you have no figure in mind; you leave the amount to the agent. If the agent explains that something has to be recorded or adjusted on your order before the amount can be given, you say that is fine and let them do it, without asking for details. Once the agent tells you the amount and hands you the payment step, you pay that exact amount by card yourself, and if asked how you are paying you say card. After the payment goes through you thank the agent briefly and say goodbye; you do not ask for anything else. You never mention your old insurance claim, any warranty, any missed appointment or any credit unless the agent asks you directly, and then you only confirm what the agent reads to you.
